intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-43 (MRT43) is caused by homozygous mutation in the WASHC4 gene (KIAA1033) on chromosome 12q23.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-43 (MRT43) is caused by homozygous mutation in the WASHC4 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, our findings suggest that SWIP is a novel gene for ARID.
checks.explanation: The abstract names SWIP as a candidate gene for ARID, found by homozygosity mapping in a consanguineous family. It does not explicitly say the mutation was homozygous, and it does not use the MRT43 designation or the WASHC4 symbol.

checks.claim: WASHC4 is also known as KIAA1033.
checks.evidence_quote: Novel KIAA1033/WASHC4 mutations in three patients with syndromic intellectual disability
checks.explanation: The paper uses KIAA1033 and WASHC4 as names for the same gene.

checks.claim: The WASHC4 gene is located on chromosome 12q23.
checks.evidence_quote: In 2011, KIAA1033/WASHC4 was associated with autosomal recessive intellectual disability (ARID)
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosomal location. Under the stated rule, a standard location restating a gene the paper names counts as supported.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-43 (MRT43) is a nonsyndromic form of intellectual disability. It is caused by loss of function of SWIP (WASHC4), a subunit of the WASH complex, which regulates actin polymerization at endosomes and endosomal trafficking.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-43 (MRT43) is a nonsyndromic form of intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: Identification of a novel candidate gene for non-syndromic autosomal recessive intellectual disability: the WASH complex member SWIP.
checks.explanation: The title states that the intellectual disability is non-syndromic.

checks.claim: MRT43 is caused by loss of function of SWIP (WASHC4).
checks.evidence_quote: the data presented here support a mechanistic model whereby SWIPP1019R causes a loss of WASH complex function
checks.explanation: Paper frames the patient mutation as loss of function.

checks.claim: SWIP (WASHC4) is a subunit of the WASH complex.
checks.evidence_quote: a member of the recently discovered WASH complex
checks.explanation: The abstract states that SWIP is a member of the WASH complex.

checks.claim: The WASH complex regulates actin polymerization at endosomes.
checks.evidence_quote: activating Arp2/3-dependent actin branching at the outer surface of endosomes to influence cargo sorting and vesicular scission
checks.explanation: Directly stated.

checks.claim: The WASH complex regulates endosomal trafficking.
checks.evidence_quote: which is involved in actin polymerization and multiple endosomal transport processes
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the WASH complex is involved in endosomal transport.

paragraphs.text: Ropers et al. (2011) reported a large consanguineous Iranian family in which several members had nonsyndromic intellectual disability that was inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.

checks.claim: Ropers et al. (2011) reported a large consanguineous Iranian family in which several members had nonsyndromic intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: In a large consanguineous family with autosomal recessive intellectual disability (ARID)
checks.explanation: The abstract does not say the family is Iranian; the full text may state it.

checks.claim: The nonsyndromic intellectual disability in the large consanguineous Iranian family reported by Ropers et al. (2011) was inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern.
checks.evidence_quote: In a large consanguineous family with autosomal recessive intellectual disability (ARID)
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the disorder in this family as autosomal recessive.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of MRT43 in the family reported by Ropers et al. (2011) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of MRT43 in the family reported by Ropers et al. (2011) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: In a large consanguineous family with autosomal recessive intellectual disability (ARID)
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the inheritance in this family as autosomal recessive.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous Iranian family with intellectual disability, Ropers et al. (2011) found a homozygous mutation in the KIAA1033 gene, which encodes SWIP (WASHC4). They identified it by linkage mapping followed by sequencing of candidate genes. The mutation segregated with the disorder in the family. Patient cells had lower levels of SWIP and of other WASH complex subunits, which suggested that the mutation destabilizes the WASH complex.

checks.claim: Ropers et al. (2011) found a homozygous mutation in the KIAA1033 gene in affected members of a consanguineous Iranian family with intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: we have combined homozygosity mapping, targeted exon enrichment and high-throughput sequencing to identify the underlying gene defect
checks.explanation: The abstract does not say the family is Iranian, does not state homozygosity explicitly and does not use the name KIAA1033. It refers only to the SWIP gene.

checks.claim: The KIAA1033 gene encodes SWIP (WASHC4).
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention KIAA1033.

checks.claim: Ropers et al. (2011) identified the KIAA1033 mutation in the Iranian family by linkage mapping followed by sequencing of candidate genes.
checks.evidence_quote: we have combined homozygosity mapping, targeted exon enrichment and high-throughput sequencing to identify the underlying gene defect
checks.explanation: The abstract describes homozygosity mapping followed by targeted exon enrichment and high-throughput sequencing, then SNP filtering. That is not the same as sequencing selected candidate genes, so the draft's description of the method is inaccurate.

checks.claim: The KIAA1033 mutation segregated with intellectual disability in the Iranian family reported by Ropers et al. (2011).
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention segregation; this may be in the full text.

checks.claim: Cells from patients with the homozygous KIAA1033 mutation had lower levels of SWIP.
checks.evidence_quote: we could show that this mutation leads to significantly reduced SWIP levels
checks.explanation: The abstract reports reduced SWIP levels. It does not say patient cells were used, but the claim follows from the stated finding.

checks.claim: Cells from patients with the homozygous KIAA1033 mutation had lower levels of other WASH complex subunits.
checks.evidence_quote: leads to significantly reduced SWIP levels and to destabilization of the entire WASH complex
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions destabilization of the whole complex. It does not specifically report lower levels of the other subunits.

checks.claim: The reduced levels of WASH complex subunits in patient cells suggested that the KIAA1033 mutation destabilizes the WASH complex.
checks.evidence_quote: this mutation leads to significantly reduced SWIP levels and to destabilization of the entire WASH complex
checks.explanation: The abstract concludes that the mutation destabilizes the WASH complex.

paragraphs.text: Courtland et al. (2021) made knockin mice carrying the Swip mutation that corresponds to the human P1019R mutation. The mutant mice had less WASH complex. Their neurons showed endolysosomal abnormalities, and the mice developed cognitive and motor deficits.

checks.claim: Courtland et al. (2021) made knockin mice carrying the Swip mutation that corresponds to the human P1019R mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Due to the sequence homology of human and mouse Washc4 genes, we were able to introduce the same point mutation in exon 29 of murine Washc4 using CRISPR
checks.explanation: CRISPR knockin of the P1019R-equivalent mutation.

checks.claim: Swip P1019R knockin mice had less WASH complex.
checks.evidence_quote: displayed significantly decreased abundance of two WASH complex members, Strumpellin and WASH1 (Figure 2B). These results phenocopied data from the human patients
checks.explanation: Reduced WASH complex components in mutant brain.

checks.claim: Neurons of Swip P1019R knockin mice showed endolysosomal abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: These data support the finding that the SWIPP1019R mutation results in both molecular and morphological abnormalities in the endo-lysosomal pathway.
checks.explanation: Shown in cultured mutant neurons and in vivo.

checks.claim: Swip P1019R knockin mice developed cognitive deficits.
checks.evidence_quote: MUT mice displayed a significant deficit in cued fear memory
checks.explanation: Cognitive deficit shown by fear conditioning.

checks.claim: Swip P1019R knockin mice developed motor deficits.
checks.evidence_quote: These findings demonstrate that SWIPP1019R results in progressive motor function decline
checks.explanation: Rotarod and gait deficits.

paragraphs.text: Ropers et al. (2011) found a homozygous c.3056C-G transversion in the KIAA1033 (WASHC4) gene in affected members of a consanguineous Iranian family with nonsyndromic intellectual disability (MRT43). It results in a pro1019-to-arg (P1019R) substitution. The mutation segregated with the disorder and reduced the levels of the WASH complex in patient cells.

checks.claim: Ropers et al. (2011) found a homozygous c.3056C-G transversion in the KIAA1033 (WASHC4) gene in affected members of a consanguineous Iranian family with nonsyndromic intellectual disability (MRT43).
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the c.3056C-G variant, zygosity or Iranian origin; the abstract does not specify the variant, which would be in the full text.

checks.claim: The KIAA1033 c.3056C-G transversion results in a pro1019-to-arg (P1019R) substitution.
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions only a non-synonymous change and does not give the P1019R substitution.

checks.claim: The KIAA1033 P1019R mutation segregated with intellectual disability in the Iranian family.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention segregation.

checks.claim: The KIAA1033 P1019R mutation reduced the levels of the WASH complex in patient cells.
checks.evidence_quote: this mutation leads to significantly reduced SWIP levels and to destabilization of the entire WASH complex
checks.explanation: The abstract reports destabilization of the complex but does not specify patient cells or name the variant.
